objective: Test whether a conservative output-consistency router can retain checkpoint-16 precision while accepting only structurally bounded changes from the recall-heavier 75% on-policy repair bridge.

study_scope.design_disclosure: The policy family was designed after inspecting the signed convex-bridge failure and its 21 changed rows. Fresh cross-fit measures fold consistency but is not independent evidence.

frozen_inputs.v9_reference: The same hash-bound memory-condition outputs used by the checkpoint and bridge studies.

policies.rule: Use the proposal only when its boundary set is a strict subset of the checkpoint boundary set.
Use the proposal only when checkpoint 16 predicts an empty set and the proposal predicts exactly one boundary.
Use the proposal when either the strict-subset rule or the abstention-singleton rule fires; otherwise use checkpoint 16.

evaluation.source: The same 220 open publisher-TRAIN-derived scene development rows used by the preceding adaptive studies.
evaluation.per_fold_selection: On the other four folds, rank the four policies by scene micro-F1 descending, precision descending, recall descending, then locked candidate order; apply the winner only to the held-out fold.

deployment_tradeoff: The router is dual-pass and optimizes benchmark quality, not latency. A later distillation study may train a single-pass router only after independent evidence exists.
stopping_rule: Archive and push the protocol and signed TRAIN-only outcome. This post-hoc study cannot authorize publisher validation, publisher test, Hard32, the unused 73-row holdout, multitask preservation, or external replication.
